The corner of Newstead and Lucky, about 1921

Every footprint on these blocks was traced from the Sanborn fire-insurance atlas of St. Louis, Volume 7 (October 1909), sheets 7 and 8. The two sheets cover N. Taylor to Pendleton and Garfield to Easton. Lucky Street is today’s Aldine Avenue.

On the northwest corner, 4401 Lucky is drawn as a two-story brick store, with a one-story brick bake house and a bake oven behind it along Newstead. So a bakery stood there by 1909. You can walk into the bake house through its door on Newstead and look into the oven. The room's size and the oven's place come from the map; the door, windows, fittings and fire are a period-typical reconstruction. The map doesn’t name the owner, so the Fraundorf name on the sign comes from outside it.

Pink on the map = brickYellow = frame (wood)

What is estimated: heights are rules of thumb (brick houses 2 stories, frame houses about 1½, sheds 1), not each building’s own number. Rooflines, colours, trees, signs, vehicles and the Easton streetcar are period-typical guesses. Eleven houses that went up between 1909 and 1921 on the 4300 blocks east of Newstead are added from the National Register district inventory (nine 2-story brick houses on Cote Brilliante from 1912–13, and two 1-story brick houses at 4357–59 Lucky from 1912). Their positions come from the house numbers on the 1909 map, and their footprints are typical rather than surveyed. West of Newstead, outside the district, any building after 1909 isn’t shown. The south side of Easton is in Volume 5 of the atlas and isn’t shown here.

Map: Sanborn Map Company, St. Louis Vol. 7, 1909, Library of Congress (public domain).

VR: checking for a headset… In VR, the left stick walks (hold grip to hurry), the right stick turns in 30° steps, A jumps to the next place, B lays the 1909 map on the ground, and X switches flying on and off (the right stick then rises and sinks). You can also walk around your own room.
